commits.message: docs: review fixes — enum names in the attribute table, the export shown, deepData described, examples' own names explained, ensureDrawn drawn at 256 colours (rich-docs-examples-xuu.pt4)

docs: the text, styling and console pages show their examples' real output (rich-docs-examples-xuu.pt4)

Eleven pages come off NOT_YET_MIGRATED: introduction, console, text, markup,
style, highlighting, contrast, transpose, template-bindings, protocol,
traceback. Every example runs at build time or carries its marker; no
hand-drawn output remains.

Folded in: rich-docs-gpe (stylize argument order), rich-docs-0dh (protocol.md
now documents Segment-yielding render with yield* delegation; the richConsole
hook, which nothing reads, is gone), rich-docs-drn (markup.md states which
bracketed runs are tags, with both surprises in the output).

markup.md's doubled-backslash paragraph is removed rather than rewritten to the
port's behaviour, which is bug rich-markup-nm1.

Filed from the real output: rich-color-dhay, rich-status-o9av,
rich-table-pyrl, rich-template-bindings-4bgw.

fix(themes): every bundled theme draws named colours in its own ANSI table (rich-docs-examples-xuu.8tt) (#179)

* fix(themes): every bundled theme draws named colours in its own ANSI table (rich-docs-examples-xuu.8tt)

defineTheme gave every TerminalTheme STANDARD_TABLE, so `[blue]` exported
under ATOM_ONE_DARK was VGA #000080 on #282c34. Each theme data file now
carries a required `ansi` table, taken from the published terminal scheme
whose background matches the theme (iTerm2-Color-Schemes), from Rich for
`default` and `svg-export`, and from Textual's own MONOKAI/ALABASTER
fallback for the Textual-native themes and cyberpunk, which have none.

Atom One uses "One Half Dark/Light": the "Atom One Light" port draws cyan
as the same #3F953A as green.

* fix(themes): textual-ansi keeps VGA, derived once from STANDARD_TABLE; ANSI slots are opaque; EIGHT_BIT 0–15 draws through the theme (rich-docs-examples-xuu.8tt)
